research.job_description_summary: IBM hires freshers in India as Associate System Engineers. Glassdoor reviews describe a multi-stage process: a cognitive ability test made of games, a personality test, an English assessment (an October 2026 review lists a four-question scenario-based writing test and a 42-question listening and speaking test), a coding assessment (a 2019 review: one coding question and five MCQs in 30 minutes), technical interviews on basic programming, data structures, OOP, SQL, DBMS, networks and projects (a September 2026 review), and a final technical and HR interview. The official IBM careers pages were not fetched.
limitations: IBM's official careers pages were not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

Only three 2026 reviews on one Glassdoor page give process or topics, and none lists specific questions; the 2019 review (older than the 2025 cutoff) gives the coding-assessment format and the project 'other uses and profit' question, so those are marked low confidence.
The cognitive 'games', personality scenarios, Knockri writing test and SHL speaking test cannot be reproduced as text; items for rounds 1 to 3 are original proxies for the formats.
A September 2026 review of campus hiring in Bengaluru and an October 2026 review from Gandhinagar describe different campus processes; this bank combines them.
Reported items carry one report each and are unverified; most of the bank is original practice.
A review from 1 October 2026 said it had applied online and heard nothing; it contributed no content.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
